preamble: Spirantization of the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] to the voiced alveolar fricative [z] turns the palatal closure into an alveolar sibilant while keeping voicing. In Oti-Volta (Gur), Eddyshaw reconstructs a Proto-Oti-Volta initial *j [ɟ] that became z in Western Oti-Volta (Kusaal, Mooré, Farefare, Dagbani and their relatives) in parallel with the voiceless *c > s; Nõotre instead devoiced it to c, Core Eastern Oti-Volta weakened it to y, and Gurma and Buli keep the stop.

examples.note: Forms in Eddyshaw's transcription: j = [ɟ], y = [j], ɩ ʋ = [ɪ ʊ], a tilde below a vowel marks nasalization, ' marks a glottalized vowel; POV = Proto-Oti-Volta; the final syllable of nouns is a noun-class suffix. The front root vowel comes from umlaut generalized from the plural; Buli keeps the stop (júm), Nõotre devoices it (cìmmilá).
Buli jīuk, Moba jóól̀, Nõotre cúré.
Eddyshaw: in Western Oti-Volta *j becomes z, except in Nõotre, where it is devoiced to c.
